Root cause: Changes are pushed by email only; nothing at the point of use shows what changed
Proposed fix: Scenario A (staff read it): every circular opens with a "What changed" box (date, version, the change in one line); changes to control steps need a tick-to-acknowledge. Scenario B (staff skip it): if acknowledgement stays below target after 30 days, the change is pushed to the point of use: branch managers brief it at the morning huddle, and the assistant flags "changed on [date]" on any answer that uses it
Why this fix and not AI (or why AI): AI cannot make staff read an email; the fix is how changes are communicated
Also needs: Acknowledgement rate tracked per branch (the trigger for Scenario B)

Pain point: No quick way to tell which version is current
Root cause: Old copies live on in downloads and memory; no single source of truth
Proposed fix: One version-controlled library: one live version per procedure, old versions marked Superseded, a named owner and an effective date on every circular
Why this fix and not AI (or why AI): AI is only as reliable as the library it reads. Fix the library first
Also needs: Kamilisha cites the version in every answer

Root cause: Controls are checked after the fact at QA; no early warning
Proposed fix: Weekly QA returns dashboard by procedure and branch, so branch managers act within days, not at audit
Why this fix and not AI (or why AI): Counting and showing errors is reporting; no AI needed
Also needs: P4 and P5 rules reduce the errors at source

Pain point: Card-blocking form skipped on card replacement
Root cause: The system lets an officer block a card and capture a replacement without the signed form
Proposed fix: System hard stop: the replacement request cannot be captured until the signed blocking form is scanned. Supervisor authorisation checks the form. Interim: printed checklist at the counter
Why this fix and not AI (or why AI): A mandatory control must be enforced by the system. Advice from an assistant can be ignored

Pain point: Business account documents list applied inconsistently
Root cause: The list changes and staff work from memory
Proposed fix: One-page documents checklist per entity type taken from the current circular; attached to every account file and checked by QA
Why this fix and not AI (or why AI): A fixed list is a checklist; no judgement is involved
Also needs: Kamilisha gives the right checklist for the entity type with its source

Pain point: Slow to find the right section
Root cause: Long circulars, keyword search, and staff ask in their own words rather than document titles
Proposed fix: Assistant that answers in short steps from the current library, with circular, section and version cited
Why this fix and not AI (or why AI): Staff questions do not match document titles; search needs exact keywords and still returns 20–50 page documents. Better search was considered (see options note) and only partly solves this
Also needs: P1 and P2 library fixes must come first

Pain point: Circulars are long, in English and full of jargon
Root cause: Written for policy accuracy rather than quick reading at the counter
Proposed fix: Same assistant gives plain English or Swahili steps, with the original text one click away
Why this fix and not AI (or why AI): Rewriting and translating every circular by hand is slow and costly to keep current. Owners should still add a plain summary to new circulars

Pain point: Training unit cannot see where staff struggle
Root cause: No record of what staff ask or where they make mistakes
Proposed fix: Most-asked questions dashboard from the assistant's question log, plus QA returns by procedure (P3) as an early signal
Why this fix and not AI (or why AI): Counting questions is reporting. It depends on the P6 assistant for the question log; the QA dashboard gives a signal now
Also needs: Question log built into the assistant
